chunks: From him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Amr ibn Shimr, from Jabir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Allah hates the obscene, the vulgar, and the insistent beggar.'

key_terms.الْبَذِي‏ءَ: The vulgar one (one who is coarse or lowly in manner)
key_terms.الْفَاحِشَ: The obscene one (one who is indecent in speech or action)
key_terms.الْمُلْحِفَ: The insistent one (who persists in asking)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people Allah hates according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi’s chapter on obscenities, this hadith links linguistic vulgarity with social dependency, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *adab* (etiquette) as a reflection of inner purity. The term *al-mulhif* specifically denotes one who begs persistently to the point of annoyance, highlighting the dignity of self-sufficiency. This teaching underscores the holistic nature of character in Shia ethics, where speech and social behavior are equally scrutinized.
